name: Roskilde University
about: Roskilde University was set up in 1972 to experiment with how knowledge is taught, and it still works differently from every other Danish university. You do not apply to a named subject. You apply to one of three broad international bachelor programmes, spend the whole first year in an interdisciplinary basic studies section, and only then choose the two bachelor subjects you will study for the remaining two years. Roughly half of all study time is group project work on real problems rather than lectures and exams, and the campus at Trekroner, 30 minutes by train from Copenhagen, has about 7,900 students.

languageOfInstruction.note: RUC's structure is the thing to understand before applying. You apply to a broad programme, not to a named subject. Year one is a shared interdisciplinary basic studies section; years two and three are spent on two bachelor subjects you choose at the end of year one. Your degree title is the combination.

notes: RUC's structure is the thing to understand before applying. You apply to a broad programme, not to a named subject. Year one is a shared interdisciplinary basic studies section; years two and three are spent on two bachelor subjects you choose at the end of year one. Your degree title is the combination.
Individual bachelor subjects can have additional entry requirements. Check RUC’s separate subject requirements before deciding what you want to combine.
About half of all study time at RUC is group project work rather than taught classes and written exams.

RUC lists indicative teaching hours, not an automatic hours-only test of equivalence. For IB applicants, use its published IB subject conversion table; IB applicants do not need to submit the standard verification form.
RUC’s published guaranteed-admission thresholds are for 2026 only. For 2027, do not treat these figures or historical quota 1 cutoffs as entry requirements.
RUC does not accept English language tests in place of Danish-level English B. Use RUC’s IB subject conversion table to check your English course.

Apply via Optagelse.dk from 1 February to 15 March 2027 at noon (Denmark time). If you are finishing the IB in 2027, RUC’s published deadline for the final qualification is 5 July at noon; other documents are normally due 15 March. For the full Diploma route, provide both the final IB transcript and the Diploma. RUC publishes separate deadlines for supplementary subjects.
RUC’s 2027 undergraduate open house is on 11 February, 13:00–18:00, on campus. No registration is required.

EU, EEA and Swiss citizens pay no application fee or tuition. For fee-paying students, RUC’s published rates for entry from September 2026 are EUR 10,000 per year for Global Humanities or Social Sciences and EUR 16,000 for Natural Sciences. Check the 2027 rate and any residence-permit exemption with RUC. The separate application fee is EUR 200 unless exempt.

You apply to one of three broad international bachelor programmes, spend the whole first year in an interdisciplinary basic studies section, and only then choose the two bachelor subjects you will study for the remaining two years. Roughly half of all study time is group project work on real problems rather than lectures and exams, and the campus at Trekroner, 30 minutes by train from Copenhagen, has about 7,900 students.

programmes.about: The first year covers the humanities in four broad dimensions — culture, text, history and subjectivity — before you choose two bachelor subjects from Communication Studies, Cultural Encounters, Social Psychology of Everyday Life, Business Studies and International Studies. It suits students interested in culture, media and how people make sense of the world, and who want to combine that with something applied.

requirements.label: A qualifying upper-secondary examination

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

sources.title: DP Course Results (formerly the IB Certificate) of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three subjects at HL, are a qualifying examination in Denmark on the same terms as a two-year hf without overbygning: they give access to erhvervsakademi- and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2, and to a university bachelor only after two successive raises of upper-secondary subject level, at least one to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag. Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.
sources.quote: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. Ansøgere med et Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results på mindst 18 point og mindst karakteren 3 i alle fag kan derudover få adgang til en universitetsbacheloruddannelse gennem kvote 1 og 2 ved enten at supplere med enkeltfag efter samme regler som hf’erne eller tage deres IB-eksamen om for at få et IB Diploma – Retake.

alternativeRouteSummary.short: Course Results of 18+ points (grade 3 in all six, three at HL) count once you raise two subjects a level, one of them to A level. Or retake for the Diploma.
